reasons: No Composio managed app exists for Clover

scenarios.label: Sandbox build and testing only
scenarios.when_this_applies: You only build and test in the Clover sandbox, with no outside merchants.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: Account approval is not needed for sandbox-only use (c1).

scenarios.approval: No developer account approval needed for sandbox-only use.

scenarios.label: Production app for outside merchants
scenarios.when_this_applies: You want merchants outside your company to connect through a production app, typically listed on the Clover App Market.

hands_on.basis: estimate from steps: identity and business documents, functional video, listing content

waiting.basis: Docs give no fixed review time (c14); only a 10-business-day document deadline (c10) and one 7-week report (c15).

prerequisites.title: Owner role on developer account
prerequisites.detail: Only an owner can view and edit account settings and accept the Clover Developer Agreement.

prerequisites.title: Identity and business documents
prerequisites.detail: Have ID (passport, or driver's license in Canada/UK), proof of address, and for companies an EIN/Tax ID plus proof of business address ready.

prerequisites.title: Own OAuth app credentials
prerequisites.detail: Composio has no managed app for Clover, so you must supply your own client ID and secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config via Composio's API with your Clover client ID and secret, using the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a test connection works in sandbox.

steps.title: Fill in developer account details
steps.detail: On the production environment, open Developer Settings, enter each section, and click Verify Your Account. Use the Business type for a company.

steps.title: Respond to document requests
steps.detail: Upload requested documents to the secure folder, not by email, within 10 business days.

steps.title: Wait for account approval
steps.detail: Clover verifies identity and company details and runs an OFAC check. No timeline is published.

steps.title: Draft use case and test redirects
steps.detail: Draft the primary use case description and a video script, and check the app uses Production, not Sandbox, with working redirect links.
steps.done_when: Description and script are ready for review.

steps.title: Record video and submit app
steps.detail: Record the functional video, enter its URL and description, finish the Submission Checklist, and click Submit for Approval.

steps.title: Wait for App Market review
steps.detail: If it runs long, contact Developer Relations. If denied with no reason, reply to the rejection email thread.
steps.done_when: App is approved or you have a rejection reason.

traps.title: No published review timeline
traps.detail: Clover gives no fixed review time. One developer reported 7 weeks with no response, so plan launch dates with slack.

traps.title: Sandbox left on in production code
traps.detail: Leaving the code on Sandbox instead of Production, or a broken redirect link, are the most frequent functional rejection causes.

traps.title: Document deadline
traps.detail: Requested verification documents must arrive within 10 business days or the application may be rejected.

traps.title: Other payment processors
traps.detail: Clover allows transactions only through its own network, so apps using another processor risk rejection.

blockers.symptom: Verify your Developer Account banner on Production

blockers.what_it_means: Clover denied the app without detail.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: At Clover, we frequently see three categories in which apps are rejected:
evidence.answer: Clover's developer advocate says apps are most often rejected in three areas: Legal and Privacy, Market Listing, and App Testing (Functional).

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: App functionality is one of the top reasons for app rejections.
evidence.answer: Functional problems are among the top causes of rejection, and common ones include environment mix-ups and broken redirects.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Most errors occur because of not changing the environment — Sandbox versus Production — in the code, or a broken link in the redirect.
evidence.answer: The most frequent functional blockers are leaving the app on Sandbox instead of Production and a broken redirect link.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Clover only allows applications to handle and process transactions through the Clover network.
evidence.answer: Apps that process payments through another processor are a rejection risk, since only Clover network processing is allowed.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: I submitted my application to the Clover App Market 7 weeks ago and it has been radio silence.
evidence.answer: Developer report (a single LinkedIn post, about two years old): an App Market submission sat about 7 weeks with no response, and the developer said follow-up emails to support went unanswered.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: App approval timelines can vary, but if your app has been under review for an extended period, it's recommended to contact Clover Developer Relations directly for a status update.
evidence.answer: Clover publishes no fixed review time; its docs tell developers to contact Developer Relations when a review runs long.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Reply directly to the rejection email thread—this often prompts a response with the reason for denial.
evidence.answer: If a denial comes without a reason, replying to the rejection email thread is the suggested way to get the reason.
